where: Théorème 6.1, 'Pour S' convenable, A_η' a réduction stable'
scan: A_{η'} a réduction stable (a prime typed after the subscript η; no comma before 'a')
note: The mark after the subscript η is a prime, not a comma: in the PDF scan and in the DjVu witness its bitmap is the straight wedge of the two primes of 𝒜°_{S's'} on the same line, while the comma after 'convenable' has the hooked tail; it stands at comma height only because a prime typed at subscript level does. p. 20 introduces A_{η'} for the abelian variety deduced over η', and the verb 'a' follows its subject without a comma. One edit: adds the prime and removes the comma that was read into it.

where: 6.5, 'Rappelons que V_ℓ(A*) et V_ℓ(A) (donc V_ℓ(A*)^I et V_ℓ(A)_I sont en dualité ...'
scan: (donc V_ℓ(A*)^I et V_ℓ(A)_I sont en dualité à valeurs dans Q_ℓ(1).
note: Unbalanced parenthesis in the print: '(donc ...' is never closed; it closes after V_ℓ(A)_I, before the verb. Same in the DjVu witness. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

scan: constant sur S_i - D . (no index on D)
note: Missing index: in 1.3, whose notation is taken up here, D_i ⊂ S_i is the divisor π = 0 and the sheaves live on S_i - D_i; the next sentence has π_1(S_i - D_i , η̄). The spot is clean in the PDF scan and the DjVu witness has no index either. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: 6.7, display after 'On a alors par (1.3.1) :', last term
scan: T_ℓ(A)^I = T_ℓ(A^{I_i}) (the exponent I_i typed inside the parenthesis)
note: The display pairs T_ℓ(A)_I = T_ℓ(A)_{I_i} with T_ℓ(A)^I = T_ℓ(A)^{I_i} (invariants of the Tate module under I_i); the closing parenthesis is typed after the exponent. Low because T_ℓ(A^{I_i}) can be read as the Tate module of the I_i-invariant points, which is the same group. Same in the DjVu witness. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.
